entries.gave: Read the Cut, its decisions and the one More kept (code N8: a quotation mark that never closes ends in a _csv.Error traceback in a long file, and hides the mark in a short one), and invoicer as it stands: command.py, lines.py, render.py, totals.py, tax.py, pyproject.toml, .gitignore and the tests. Its people are the accounting colleagues, who run `invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT` on a file saved from their spreadsheet and get the invoice printed, or one line saying what to fix, and the developers and code that use the package. lines.py reads with csv.reader, which raises _csv.Error for an unclosed quote in a long file and, in a short one, reads the rest of the file into one cell, so the refusal names a later fault or none.
Read code best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-code best-practice.md, to their end before any change.

Decided: take the Cut decision "a wrong line" as it stands; in lines.py read rows by csv.reader with strict=True, through one generator _rows that numbers rows as the spreadsheet does and turns csv.Error into LineError naming the row where the quoted cell opens, with a message to remove the mark or close the cell. Settled by the purpose: a cell with text after its closing mark, such as "Pro" x, is refused by the same message, as it reads in no one way and a spreadsheet never saves it. No asks.
